page.layout: One page of text, single column, with a running head at the top; no margin notes. Below the text block a rule and a centred heading, then a short paragraph with a woodcut-style initial Q and the closing lines. Printed page number 402 at top left.

main_text.p: HERI divites duriores sunt servis suis, quàm egeni. Amph. I. I. v. 12.
IN omnibus edictis boni ominis causâ præmittebant hanc formulam: BONUM FACTUM. Poen. Prol. v. 16, 45. Græci κάλὰς ἔχει apud Josephum.
Vide Formularum authorem locupletissimum Barnabam Brissonium.
OTIM solo nutu aut crepitu digitorum, si quid vellent, poscebant, aut significabant. Aul. 4. I. v. 13.

p.i: Herile imperium edisçat, ut quod frons velit, oculi sciant.
Trimalcio lautissimus homo, digitos concrepuit, ad quod signum matellam stado ludenti suppositum.
Dum poscor crepitu digitorum, ac verna moratur, O quoties pollex culcita falsa mea est!
Cum peteret feram media jam nocte matellam Arguto madidum pollice Panarettus.
Digiti crepantis signa novit Eunuchus Et delicatæ suscitator urinæ Domini bibentis ebrium regit penem.

main_text.head: MARIS. FLUVIORUM.
main_text.p: QUISNAM istic fluvius est, quem non recipiat mare? Curc. I. I. v. 86.
MARITIMI morus à maris inconstantiâ dicti. Cist. 2. I. v. 11.

page.notes: The text is set in a mix of roman and italic with Greek words; the Greek phrase in the Josephus reference is rendered approximately. Lines near the right edge are partly faint. The woodcut initial Q is read as Q.
